entries.title: CAIDA Internet Measurement Datasets
entries.description: The dataset collection of the Center for Applied Internet Data Analysis (CAIDA) at UC San Diego: Internet topology (Ark traceroute, ITDK), BGP-derived AS relationships and prefix-to-AS mappings, network telescope and anonymized passive traces, among others. Some are public; many need an approved request.
entries.publisher: Center for Applied Internet Data Analysis (CAIDA), University of California San Diego

access.auth_note: Publicly accessible datasets download under the Public AUA; most other datasets need a data request approved by CAIDA under the Master AUA (one-year licence, CAIDA may refuse). Per-dataset access level is shown in the catalog

coverage.spatial: global Internet (topology, routing and traffic observed from CAIDA vantage points)
coverage.temporal: varies by dataset (e.g. pfx2as daily from 2005-05-09 for IPv4, 2007-01-01 for IPv6)

entries.license: restricted — CAIDA Acceptable Use Agreements: Public AUA (limited, non-exclusive, terminable licence; citation and publication reporting required) or Master AUA (non-profit research/education, commercial internal evaluation, or US Government purposes only)
entries.attribution: The CAIDA UCSD [Dataset Name] - [dates used], https://catalog.caida.org/dataset/[dataset-URL]
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (needed headless Chromium to render the listing). The old address https://www.caida.org/catalog/datasets/ redirects here. The catalog search page shows "Displaying 116 of 116" datasets with an Access filter (11 values) and a Status filter (84 "complete"). A sample dataset page, Routeviews Prefix to AS mappings (https://www.caida.org/catalog/datasets/routeviews-prefix2as/, HTTP 200), says "Files are created on a daily basis, starting from 2005-05-09 for IPv4 and 2007-01-01 for IPv6" in a tab-separated, line-oriented format, and "You are required to report your publications using this dataset to CAIDA." CAIDA is a research unit of UC San Diego (a university, not a federal agency), so this is not a US Government work. The "text" format reflects only the pfx2as sample; formats vary by dataset and were not surveyed. Cadence "irregular" because datasets update on different schedules.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the Master AUA (https://www.caida.org/about/legal/aua/) "applies to the majority of the CAIDA datasets, with the exception of datasets covered by the Acceptable Use Agreement for Publicly Accessible Datasets (Public-AUA)". It grants "a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, and terminable license to copy, modify, and use the data ... solely for the purpose of non-profit research, non-profit education, commercial internal testing and evaluation of the data, or for government purposes by or on behalf of the U.S. Government", effective "for a period of one year". The Public AUA (https://www.caida.org/about/legal/aua/public_aua/) grants "a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, and terminable license to copy, modify, and use the data in accordance with this Public Agreement" and requires the citation above plus reporting each publication to CAIDA. Neither is an open licence. Not checked: which datasets fall under which AUA, the request workflow, or any download limits.

entries.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog
entries.description: CISA's authoritative list of vulnerabilities known to be exploited in the wild, each with its CVE ID, vendor and product, date added, required action and due date, and known ransomware use. US federal agencies must remediate listed entries under Binding Operational Directive 22-01; it is widely used as a patch-priority signal.
entries.publisher: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), US Department of Homeland Security

coverage.spatial: global (vulnerabilities in products from any country, exploitation observed worldwide)
coverage.temporal: 2021-present (start year from the BOD 22-01 launch; not checked in the data)

entries.license: CC0-1.0 (KEV licence file, cisa.gov/sites/default/files/licenses/kev/license.txt)
entries.attribution: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 in headless Chromium; plain curl got HTTP 403 even with a browser User-Agent. The page says "CISA maintains the authoritative source of vulnerabilities that have been exploited in the wild", "The KEV catalog is also available in these formats: CSV JSON", links a "JSON Schema (updated 09-02-2026)" and a "License", and shows "Showing 1 to 20 of 1766 results". The JSON feed (https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/feeds/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.json) returned HTTP 200 to curl with "catalogVersion": "2026.10.30", "dateReleased": "2026-10-30T17:02:45.3665Z", "count": 1766. The CSV is at https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/csv/known_exploited_vulnerabilities.csv (not downloaded). Cadence is "irregular" because entries are added as exploitation is confirmed, often several times a week. The 2021 start and the BOD 22-01 description are from background knowledge, not from pages read this session.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: https://www.cisa.gov/sites/default/files/licenses/kev/license.txt (403 to curl, HTTP 200 in headless Chromium): "The KEV database is distributed under the Creative Commons 0 1.0 License. You may use this data in any legal manner but note that information provided at any 3rd party links included in the KEV database are bound by the policies and licenses of those 3rd party websites. Use of the information does not authorize you to use the CISA Logo or DHS Seal". This is data-specific; as a federal agency work it would be public domain in the US anyway, and CC0 extends that worldwide.

entries.title: Cloudflare Radar Internet Traffic and Security Data
entries.description: Aggregate Internet trends observed across Cloudflare's network, served through the Radar API: HTTP request and NetFlow traffic, application- and network-layer attacks, BGP anomalies, DNS, and domain rankings, by country and network. A company-run source with an explicit (non-commercial) data licence.
entries.publisher: Cloudflare, Inc. (Cloudflare Radar)

access.auth_note: Free Cloudflare API token with Account > Radar > Read permission ("you must obtain your API token first")

coverage.spatial: global (traffic seen by Cloudflare's network; by country, region and autonomous system)
coverage.temporal: not checked

entries.license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Cloudflare Radar developer documentation, data-specific statement)
entries.attribution: Cloudflare Radar
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for the Radar developer documentation (https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/), which says "Using Radar's API you can access Cloudflare's data on global Internet traffic. Radar's API is free, allowing academics, technology professionals, and other web enthusiasts to investigate Internet usage across the globe." Its menu lists HTTP requests, NetFlows, application- and network-layer attacks, BGP anomalies (Beta), DNS and Domains ranking. The public dashboard https://radar.cloudflare.com/ returned HTTP 403 to curl and to headless Chromium ("Performing security verification ... protect against malicious bots"), so the docs page is catalogued as the canonical URL; the link checker will likely also be challenged on the dashboard. "Make your first API request" (https://developers.cloudflare.com/radar/get-started/first-request/) says requests go to https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/radar/ with a Bearer token and shows format=json and format=csv parameters. Cloudflare is a commercial company, not a public body; jurisdiction national/US records its legal seat only, since the schema has no value for a company. Cadence "daily" is a placeholder; Radar data is near-real-time and the aggregation intervals were not checked. No API call was made (no token), so the history depth and rate limits are unknown.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the same docs page states "Data available via Radar API endpoints is made available under the CC BY-NC 4.0 license." This is explicit and data-specific, but non-commercial; it was found on the developer docs, not on the radar.cloudflare.com dashboard, which could not be read.

entries.title: Common Crawl Web Crawl Archives
entries.description: Monthly open crawls of the public web (about 2 billion pages and over 100 TiB compressed per crawl) as raw WARC captures, WAT metadata and WET extracted text, with CDXJ/URL indexes and host- and domain-level web graphs. A widely cited snapshot series of the web itself.
entries.publisher: Common Crawl Foundation

coverage.spatial: global (public web pages fetched by CCBot)
coverage.temporal: monthly archives 2013-present on the archive index page (latest CC-MAIN-2026-43, October 2026); earlier crawls not checked

entries.license: unverified — Common Crawl Terms of Use (rev. March 7, 2024) grant a "limited, non-assignable, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive" licence to use the Service; crawled pages "may be subject to separate terms" from their owners; no open data licence named
entries.attribution: Common Crawl Foundation, Common Crawl <crawl ID, e.g. CC-MAIN-2026-43>
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The Get Started page says the data "is hosted by Amazon Web Services' Open Data Sets Sponsorships program on the bucket s3://commoncrawl/, located in the US-East-1 (Northern Virginia) AWS Region. You may process the data in the AWS cloud or download it for free over HTTP(S)". The Latest Crawl page (https://commoncrawl.org/latest-crawl, HTTP 200) states "The latest crawl is: CC-MAIN-2026-43" and offers gzipped path lists of "WARC, WAT and WET files". The archive index (https://data.commoncrawl.org/crawl-data/index.html, HTTP 200), titled "Common Crawl Archives 2013-2026", says "The archives of the main crawl are released on a monthly basis" and lists CC-MAIN-2026-43 (October 2026, 2.16 billion pages, 109.20 TiB compressed). The site menu also lists a CDXJ Index, URL Index and Web Graphs; these were not opened. The Common Crawl Foundation is a US non-profit running a global crawl, recorded as international-ngo. The Internet Archive's Wayback CDX API was considered as a sibling entry but not written here.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Terms of Use, "LAST UPDATED: March 7, 2024" (https://commoncrawl.org/terms-of-use). "1. LIMITED LICENSE CC grants you a limited, non-assignable, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive, limited license to access and use the Service subject to the terms and conditions of these ToU." It adds that the "Crawled Content" "may be subject to separate terms of use or terms of service from the owners of such Crawled Content", and lists prohibited uses (e.g. harvesting personal information, breaking the law). This is a service licence, not an open data licence, and the copyright in crawled pages stays with their owners, so re-users must check both. Not checked: rate limits on data.commoncrawl.org, the web-graph and index formats in detail, and the pre-2013 crawls.

entries.title: CRAN Package Repository Metadata
entries.description: Machine-readable indexes of all packages on CRAN, the Comprehensive R Archive Network (DESCRIPTION fields such as version, licence, dependencies, maintainer and publication date, in packages.rds and the PACKAGES index), alongside daily check results and the archive of past versions. The authoritative record of the R package ecosystem.
entries.publisher: CRAN team (Comprehensive R Archive Network), with resources of the R Foundation and WU Wien

coverage.spatial: global (packages submitted to CRAN)
coverage.temporal: current packages in the indexes; earlier versions in the Archive directory; start year not checked

entries.license: unverified — no licence or terms found for CRAN's own metadata files; each package carries its own licence in its DESCRIPTION file
entries.attribution: CRAN, the Comprehensive R Archive Network (https://CRAN.R-project.org)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page says "Currently, the CRAN package repository features 25610 available packages", links tables "sorted by date of publication" and "by name", "CRAN Task Views" ("Currently, 50 views are available"), check results, and the "Archive" of "Previous versions of the packages". HEAD requests returned HTTP 200 for https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/packages.rds (12,699,068 bytes, last-modified Sat, 31 Oct 2026 21:30:28 GMT) and https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES.gz (1,965,157 bytes, same evening). Their field lists were not opened; packages.rds is an R serialised data frame and PACKAGES is Debian control (DCF) format. The CRAN Repository Policy (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/policies.html) says "CRAN is maintained by the efforts of volunteers (the "CRAN team") and the resources of the R Foundation and the employers of those volunteers (WU Wien, TU Dortmund, U Oxford, U Auckland)". The R Foundation is based in Vienna, but CRAN is a volunteer, multi-institution network, so it is recorded as international-ngo. The CRAN mirror network and download logs (e.g. the RStudio/Posit CRAN mirror logs) are not part of this entry. Cadence "daily" is a floor: the index files were regenerated on the day of checking.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: none found. The Repository Policy addresses package licences ("The package's license must give the right for CRAN to distribute the package in perpetuity") but says nothing about re-use of CRAN's index or metadata files, and no terms page was found on cran.r-project.org. The metadata is largely author-supplied DESCRIPTION text, including maintainer names and email addresses.

entries.title: ENISA European Vulnerability Database (EUVD)
entries.description: The EU's vulnerability database, maintained by ENISA under the NIS2 Directive: publicly known vulnerabilities in ICT products and services with EUVD and alias identifiers (CVE, GHSA), CVSS scores, EPSS exploitation probability, exploited-in-the-wild flags and vendor data, including those coordinated by EU CSIRTs.
entries.publisher: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA)

access.rate_limit: API responses capped at 100 records per search request (8 for the front-page endpoints); no request-rate limit stated

coverage.spatial: global (ICT products and services), with an EU CSIRT coordination focus
coverage.temporal: not checked

entries.license: unverified — no data-specific licence; ENISA website legal notice (site-wide) says "Reproduction of ENISA material published on this website is authorized, provided the source is acknowledged, unless it is stated otherwise"; much of the content is integrated from MITRE CVE and other sources
entries.attribution: European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), European Vulnerability Database (EUVD)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for the HTML shell, but the page is a JavaScript app ("You need to enable JavaScript to run this app") and its contents needed headless Chromium. Rendered, it shows lists of "Critical vulnerabilities", "Exploited vulnerabilities" and "EU CSIRT coordinated vulnerabilities" updated within the last hours (e.g. EUVD-2026-114730, changed "1 hour ago"). The About page says "As per the NIS2 Directive, ENISA is mandated to develop and maintain the European vulnerability database", and the FAQ says it integrates data from "MITRE's federated CVE Program", vendor advisories and "CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerability Catalogue". The API page (https://euvd.enisa.europa.eu/apidoc) states "All endpoints are GET, require no authentication" with base URL https://euvdservices.enisa.europa.eu; a call to /api/lastvulnerabilities returned HTTP 200 application/json. No bulk download was found. Not checked: how far back records go, whether the record count matches CVE, and any rate limit beyond the per-request record caps.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no licence is shown on the EUVD pages or API docs. The EUVD footer links ENISA's Legal Notice (https://enisa.europa.eu/about-enisa/legal-notice/legal-notice, redirects to https://www.enisa.europa.eu/about-enisa/legal-notice), which covers "data, text, software and multimedia" on "the ENISA website" and says "Reproduction of ENISA material published on this website is authorized, provided the source is acknowledged, unless it is stated otherwise." It also says "the general principle is free access under open licenses" under ENISA's IPR policy, without naming one. This is site-wide, not EUVD-specific, and does not address the third-party (CVE, vendor) content, so the licence is left unverified.

entries.title: EPO Patent Bulk Data Sets and Open Patent Services
entries.description: The European Patent Office's raw patent data products: EP bibliographic and full-text data, the European Patent Register, the worldwide bibliographic (DOCDB) and legal event (INPADOC) databases, sequence listings, and Boards of Appeal decisions. The same data is available through the Open Patent Services (OPS) REST API, and it underlies Espacenet and most European patent analytics.
entries.publisher: European Patent Office (European Patent Organisation)

access.auth_note: free EPO account and subscription contract for bulk downloads; OPS needs registration and OAuth app keys (free up to 4 GB per week)
access.rate_limit: OPS: free up to 4 GB of data per week; above that an annual subscription (EUR 2 800) under the Fair use charter

coverage.spatial: European patents (EP), plus worldwide bibliographic and legal-event data from many patent offices (DOCDB, INPADOC)
coverage.temporal: varies by product (front files updated weekly; back files available)

entries.license: EPO terms and conditions for the licensing of EPO databases (licensed under contract with mandatory attribution; not an open licence)
entries.attribution: This product contains data sourced from EPO databases, © European Patent Organisation
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium), page "Bulk data sets | epo.org". It says "The EPO's bulk data sets are bulk extractions from EPO-internal patent databases made available to external users for further processing" and lists EP bibliographic data (EBD), the European Patent Register, EP full-text, DOCDB, INPADOC, sequence listings, national full-text data and Boards of Appeal decisions. The download platform, the Bulk Data Distribution Service (https://publication-bdds.apps.epo.org/raw-data/products, HTTP 200), needs an EPO account sign-in. Its public area listed "14.7 EPO worldwide bibliographic data (DOCDB) - front file Published at: 30.10.2026" and EP full-text data published 28.10.2026. The OPS page (https://www.epo.org/en/searching-for-patents/data/web-services/ops, HTTP 200) describes "a web service which provides access to the EPO's data via a standardised XML interface" and gives the conditions "'Non-paying' users Up to 4 GB of data per week Free" and "More than 4 GB of data per week Annual subscription: EUR 2 800". The page also points to PATSTAT for statistical analysis; PATSTAT is a separate paid product and is not cataloged here. Which bulk sets are free and which are priced was not checked, because the price list wasn't read. The XML format is assumed from the OPS documentation and DTD/Schema repository; individual product formats weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: "Terms and conditions for the licensing of EPO databases" (https://www.epo.org/en/service-support/ordering/raw-data-terms-and-conditions) says "The EPO databases are available only on a subscription basis" and "Where online access to and downloading of the EPO databases is free of charge, no payment is due". Licensees "must not use any address data included in the EPO database for advertising, promotional, spamming or other commercial purposes" and must include the statement "This product contains data sourced from EPO databases, © European Patent Organisation". The OPS terms (https://www.epo.org/en/service-support/ordering/terms-and-conditions/ops-terms-and-conditions) grant "a non-exclusive, non-transferable, worldwide licence to access OPS and use the data obtained via OPS", allow including the data in users' own products, and restrict making "the data as such" available. This is a contractual licence, not CC or public domain.

entries.title: Eurostat Digital Economy and Society Database
entries.description: Eurostat's official EU statistics on the digital economy and society, drawn mainly from the harmonised ICT usage surveys of households, individuals and enterprises. They cover internet access and use, broadband, digital skills, e-commerce, e-government, and enterprises' use of cloud, AI and other digital technologies across member states.
entries.publisher: Eurostat (European Commission)

coverage.spatial: EU member states (plus some EFTA and candidate countries)
coverage.temporal: varies by dataset (individuals' internet use series from 2002)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Eurostat copyright notice and free re-use of data)
entries.attribution: Eurostat
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium), page "Database - Digital economy and society - Eurostat", with "Comprehensive database", "Selected datasets" and "Detailed datasets" trees and tabs for Visualisations, Methodology and Legislation. The tree is collapsed in the page text, so the subject list in the description follows Eurostat's usual ICT-survey structure and wasn't read item by item. As a spot check, the dissemination API (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/isoc_ci_ifp_iu) returned JSON "Individuals - internet use", updated 2026-04-17, with time labels 2002-2025 (EU27_2020 share of individuals using the internet in the last 12 months: 94.53 for the latest year). Other formats are taken from Eurostat's general dissemination services and weren't checked. The R&D, innovation and patent tables are cataloged in science-almanac (eurostat-science-technology-innovation-database) and aren't duplicated here.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: Eurostat's copyright notice (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/help/copyright-notice) says "The copyright for the editorial content of this website, which is owned by the EU, is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence" and "Reuse of statistical data, metadata, publications, and other dissemination tools published on this website for commercial or non-commercial purposes is authorised provided the source is acknowledged." This matches the licence string used by the other Eurostat entries across the Almanac.

entries.title: FIRST Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS) Scores
entries.description: A daily probability (0 to 1, with a percentile) that each published CVE will see exploitation activity in the next 30 days, maintained by the EPSS Special Interest Group at FIRST. Used alongside CVSS and the CISA KEV catalog to prioritise patching.
entries.publisher: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST), EPSS Special Interest Group

access.rate_limit: The API docs have a "Rate Limit" section that was not read; FIRST says the API "should not be used for bulk downloads" and points to the daily CSV instead

coverage.spatial: global (all scored CVEs)
coverage.temporal: 2021-04-14-present (daily scores; model versions v1 to v5)

entries.license: unverified — no data licence named; the EPSS FAQ says scores "are published freely" with "no registration required" and "Attribution is requested"; the FIRST Services Terms of Use (site-wide) grant only a revocable licence for cybersecurity uses
entries.attribution: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST), Exploit Prediction Scoring System (EPSS), https://www.first.org/epss
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The "Get the Data" page says "A single stable URL always points to the current day's complete file" and that it is "a gzip-compressed CSV containing three fields for every scored vulnerability: cve ... epss ... percentile". It lists model versions from "EPSS v1: scores begin 2021-04-14" to "EPSS v5 (v2026.06.15): started publishing 2026-06-15", and says "Scores are generated by Empirical Security and published freely to the community." The daily file https://epss.empiricalsecurity.com/epss_scores-current.csv.gz redirected (302) to epss_scores-2026-10-31.csv.gz (HTTP 200), headed "#model_version:v2026.06.15,score_date:2026-10-31T12:00:27Z". That host belongs to Empirical Security, FIRST's named score producer, linked from FIRST's own page, so it is the official distribution and not a mirror. The API https://api.first.org/data/v1/epss?cve=CVE-2021-44228 returned JSON with "access":"public" and a 2026-10-31 score. The data page also links a GitHub repository (github.com/empiricalsec/epss_scores), which was not opened.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the EPSS FAQ (https://www.first.org/epss/faq) answers "Is EPSS free to use? Yes. EPSS scores are published freely via CSV download and API with no registration required. Attribution is requested when EPSS data is used in publications or products." No specific attribution wording was found on the data page. The FIRST Services Terms of Use, Version 1.0.0 (https://www.first.org/about/policies/terms), grant "a nonexclusive, nontransferable, revocable, limited license to view, copy, print, and distribute Content retrieved from the Services ... only for vulnerability disclosure, cybersecurity incident response, or preventative cybersecurity uses". These are site-wide, not EPSS-specific, and it is unclear whether they cover the CSV hosted by Empirical Security, so no licence id is given.

entries.title: GH Archive (Public GitHub Event Timeline)
entries.description: Hourly archives of every public GitHub event (pushes, forks, issues, pull requests, comments, releases and more) since February 2011, as gzipped JSON from the GitHub API and mirrored as a BigQuery public dataset. The standard raw source for studies of open-source developer activity.
entries.publisher: GH Archive (project maintained by Ilya Grigorik)

access.auth_note: Hourly files need no account; the BigQuery copy ("githubarchive" dataset) needs a Google Cloud project (1 TB of query processing free per month)

coverage.spatial: global (public activity on github.com)
coverage.temporal: 2011-02-12 to present (Timeline API to 2014-12-31, Events API from 2015-01-01)

entries.license: unverified — no licence stated for the event archives; the project's README licenses its code (MIT) and website text (CC-BY-4.0) only and says the dataset "includes material that may be subject to third party rights"
entries.attribution: GH Archive (www.gharchive.org)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The home page says "GH Archive is a project to record the public GitHub timeline, archive it, and make it easily accessible for further analysis", that events "are aggregated into hourly archives" at URLs like https://data.gharchive.org/2015-01-01-15.json.gz, that "Activity archives are available starting 2/12/2011", and that "The entire GH Archive is also available as a public dataset on Google BigQuery: the dataset is automatically updated every hour". A HEAD request for https://data.gharchive.org/2026-10-30-15.json.gz returned HTTP 200, so recent hours are being written. The site footer links only to github.com/igrigorik/gharchive.org; GH Archive is a long-running independent project, not a company product or a national agency, so jurisdiction international-ngo/null is the nearest schema value rather than a claim about a legal entity. The BigQuery dataset was not queried. Cadence is recorded as "daily" because the schema has no hourly value; files are written hourly.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no licence appears on www.gharchive.org. The repository README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/igrigorik/gharchive.org/master/README.md) says "MIT, for code and documentation in this repository" and "www.gharchive.org website content (gh-pages branch) is also released under CC-BY-4.0", then "Note this repository does _not_ contain the GH Archive dataset (event archives/data). The dataset includes material that may be subject to third party rights." The events themselves are GitHub API output about GitHub users' public activity, so GitHub's own terms and the users' rights may apply; this was not researched further. Treat re-use terms as unknown.

entries.title: deps.dev Open Source Insights Dependency Graph
entries.description: Resolved dependency graphs, dependents, licences, advisories and project metadata for packages in npm, PyPI, Maven, Cargo, Go, NuGet and RubyGems, rebuilt by Google from the public registries and served through a web portal, a REST API and a BigQuery public dataset with full periodic snapshots. A company-run source with an explicit licence for the data it generates.
entries.publisher: Google LLC (Open Source Insights, deps.dev)

access.auth_note: The REST API needs no key; the BigQuery dataset (bigquery-public-data.deps_dev_v1) needs a Google Cloud account (free sandbox tier, or billing for large queries)

coverage.spatial: global (public package registries and their source repositories)
coverage.temporal: not checked

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 for data deps.dev generates (resolved dependencies, advisory statistics, associations) (deps.dev BigQuery and API docs, data-specific statement); aggregated upstream registry, repository and advisory data stays under its sources' own terms
entries.attribution: deps.dev (Open Source Insights), Google; credit upstream sources (registries, GitHub/GitLab, OSV.dev, OpenSSF Scorecard) for their data
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The BigQuery documentation page says "The deps.dev BigQuery dataset provides signals that both maintainers and consumers of open-source software (OSS) can use to improve the health of their software. The dataset is provided as a BigQuery public dataset", and its sample queries read from `bigquery-public-data.deps_dev_v1.PackageVersionsLatest`. Tables listed include Advisories, Dependencies, DependencyGraphEdges, Dependents, per-ecosystem Requirements tables, PackageVersions, Projects and Snapshots ("the timestamps for which a full snapshot of all other tables exists"). The portal https://deps.dev/ also answered HTTP 200 but renders only with JavaScript ("You need to enable JavaScript to run this app"), so the docs page is catalogued instead. The API (documented at https://docs.deps.dev/api/v3/) answered HTTP 200 to an unauthenticated GET for the PyPI package "requests". The FAQ says the service "is hosted on Google Cloud Platform" and contact is depsdev@google.com; the platform "is not open source". Google is a company; jurisdiction national/US records its legal seat only. No BigQuery query was run, so the snapshot frequency and the earliest snapshot are unknown. Cadence "irregular" is a placeholder: BigQuery holds periodic full snapshots listed in a Snapshots table, frequency not checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the "Data" section of the BigQuery page (and the same text on the API v3 page) lists the upstream sources (crates.io, Go module mirror, Maven Central, npm Registry, NuGet, PyPI, RubyGems, GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, OSV.dev, OpenSSF Scorecard, OSS-Fuzz) and says "For details on using the data from these sources, please consult their documentation. Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The home page reads "A distributed vulnerability database for Open Source" and lists per-ecosystem counts (e.g. "npm 230252", "Debian 72451", "crates.io 2904"). The docs (https://google.github.io/osv.dev/data/, HTTP 200) say the sources "are aggregated and continuously exported to a GCS bucket maintained by OSV: gs://osv-vulnerabilities", with a full "all.zip", per-ecosystem all.zip files (also over HTTPS, e.g. https://storage.googleapis.com/osv-vulnerabilities/PyPI/all.zip, which answered HTTP 200 to a HEAD request), and modified_id.csv change lists. The API is documented at google.github.io/osv.dev/api/; no API call was made. The project's code lives at github.com/google/osv.dev and its docs on google.github.io, so the operator is recorded as Google; the format itself is the "OpenSSF Vulnerability format" (the OSV schema is an OpenSSF project). Google is a company; jurisdiction national/US records its legal seat only. Some ecosystem rows (Debian, the NVD conversion) are converted by the OSV team rather than published natively in OSV format. Overlaps with the CVE List and NVD by alias, but is keyed on packages and versions. Cadence "daily" is a placeholder for continuous export.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: there is no single licence for the database. The "Data sources" page (https://google.github.io/osv.dev/data/) lists each source with its licence, e.g. "GitHub Advisory Database ( CC-BY 4.0 )", "Rust Advisory Database ( CC0 1.0 )", "Ubuntu ( CC-BY-SA 4.0 )", "Chainguard / Wolfi ( CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 )", "Alpine SecDB ( CC-BY-SA 4.0 )"; the Debian and NVD conversions have no licence stated on that page. The "New Data Source" page says a contributed source's licence "must at minimum permit OSV.dev to ingest, index, modify (enrich), and publicly redistribute the records". Re-users of all.zip therefore inherit a mix of licences, including share-alike and one non-commercial/no-derivatives source; filter by ecosystem if that matters. Not checked: start year of records, the BigQuery availability (if any), and the licence of the Debian conversion.

entries.description: The Python Package Index's two public BigQuery tables: per-file download events streamed from PyPI's logs (bigquery-public-data.pypi.file_downloads) and the core metadata of every release ever uploaded (bigquery-public-data.pypi.distribution_metadata). The standard source for measuring Python package usage.
entries.publisher: Python Software Foundation (PyPI)

access.auth_note: Google Cloud account with BigQuery (the data is served from the bigquery-public-data project; free usage tier, billing for heavy queries)

coverage.spatial: global (downloads from and releases on pypi.org)
coverage.temporal: not checked

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (PyPI "BigQuery Datasets" documentation, data-specific statement)
entries.attribution: Python Software Foundation, PyPI BigQuery datasets (bigquery-public-data.pypi)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The PyPI user documentation says "We use BigQuery to serve our public datasets. PyPI offers two tables whose data is sourced from projects on PyPI." The download table "is populated through the Linehaul project by streaming download logs from PyPI to BigQuery"; the metadata table "is meant to be a data dump of metadata from every release on PyPI, which means that the rows in this BigQuery table are immutable and are not removed even if a release or project is deleted." The publisher is the PSF, not Google: pypi.org's footer reads "Developed and maintained by the Python Software Foundation and Python community"; Google only hosts the tables in its bigquery-public-data project. The PSF is a US-registered non-profit; it is recorded as international-ngo, following tech-almanac's treatment of other foundation-run global services. No BigQuery query was run, so the first date of download records and the table schemas were not checked. PyPI's JSON, Index and Stats APIs (same docs section) are not part of this entry. Cadence "daily" is a placeholder: download logs are streamed continuously.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the same page states "The tables and its pertaining data are licensed under the Creative Commons License", where the link points to https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. The licence is data-specific but named only through the link target, not spelled out as "CC BY 4.0" in the text.

entries.title: RIPE Atlas Internet Measurement Data
entries.description: Results of active Internet measurements (ping, traceroute, DNS, TLS/SSL, HTTP, NTP) run by the RIPE NCC's global network of RIPE Atlas probes and anchors, available through the RIPE Atlas API and as daily raw-data dumps.
entries.publisher: RIPE NCC (Réseaux IP Européens Network Coordination Centre)

access.auth_note: Public results can be read without an account; creating new measurements needs a RIPE NCC Access account and credits (not checked this session)

coverage.spatial: global (probe and anchor network, densest in the RIPE NCC service region of Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia)
coverage.temporal: daily dumps for roughly the last month (2026-09-30 to 2026-10-30 seen); API served 2025 results when tested, start year not checked

entries.license: restricted — RIPE Atlas Service Terms and Conditions v3.5 (research and operational use; "Any commercial use of the RIPE Atlas Data is subject to prior permission by the RIPE NCC"); no open licence named
entries.attribution: RIPE NCC, RIPE Atlas
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for https://atlas.ripe.net/ and for the RIPE NCC's RIPE Atlas page (https://www.ripe.net/analyse/internet-measurements/ripe-atlas/), whose menu lists "RIPE Atlas Raw Data" under "Raw Datasets". The daily-dump index https://data-store.ripe.net/datasets/atlas-daily-dumps/ returned HTTP 200 with folders 2026-09-30 through 2026-10-30 (latest written 31-Oct-2026); a folder holds hourly bz2 files per measurement type (e.g. "connection-2026-10-29T0000.bz2"). That index only goes back about a month, so it is a rolling window, not an archive. The RIPE NCC is the Amsterdam-based Regional Internet Registry and membership association, recorded as international-ngo. An unauthenticated API call (https://atlas.ripe.net/api/v2/measurements/1001/results/ for a one-hour window on 2025-10-31) returned HTTP 200 application/json with ping results, so the API serves results at least a year old; how far back it goes was not checked. The dump files were not decompressed, so their inner format is unconfirmed.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: RIPE Atlas Service Terms and Conditions, "Version 3.5, Updated 26 September 2025, Effective as of 4 November 2025" (https://www.ripe.net/about-us/legal/ripe-atlas-service-terms-and-conditions/). Article 4.1: "The RIPE NCC will publish the RIPE Atlas Data in various forms and make this available via http://www.ripe.net/ ... as well as the RIPE Atlas API." Article 4.5: "Users agree to make responsible use of the RIPE Atlas Data in line with the purposes of the RIPE Atlas Service ... Users may perform research using RIPE Atlas Data ... Any commercial use of the RIPE Atlas Data is subject to prior permission by the RIPE NCC." Article 3.1 gives the purposes as "research, network monitoring, network debugging and alerting about network events". No Creative Commons or other open licence was found. RIPEstat, a separate RIPE NCC service, has stricter terms (no redistribution) and is not covered here.

entries.title: crates.io Database Dumps
entries.description: Daily PostgreSQL-ready CSV dumps of all public information in the crates.io database (crates, versions, dependencies, owners, categories, keywords and download counts), with archived per-version daily downloads back to November 2014. The complete registry record for the Rust package ecosystem.
entries.publisher: Rust Foundation (crates.io team)

access.rate_limit: API: "A maximum of 1 request per second" plus an identifying User-Agent; no limits stated for the sparse index or static.crates.io

coverage.spatial: global (all crates published to crates.io)
coverage.temporal: full registry history in each dump; historical version downloads back to November 2014 (per the dump README)

entries.license: unverified — no licence for the dump data found on the Data Access Policy page or in the dump's README; the crates.io Usage Policy is CC-BY-4.0 but that covers the policy text, not the data
entries.attribution: crates.io database dump, Rust Foundation / crates.io team (<dump timestamp, e.g. 2026-10-31-020010>)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 in headless Chromium; plain curl got HTTP 403 (and 404 with a minimal browser User-Agent), because crates.io is a JavaScript app behind bot filtering, so the vertical's headless check is needed. The Data Access Policy page says "crates.io database dumps contain all information available through the crates.io API in a single download. They are updated every 24 hours. The latest dump is available at the address https://static.crates.io/db-dump.tar.gz." That URL redirects (307) to https://cloudfront-static.crates.io/db-dump.tar.gz, which answered HTTP 200 with content-length 2,118,275,837 and last-modified Sat, 31 Oct 2026 02:06:53 GMT. The first 3 MB were read: the archive root is "2026-10-31-020010/" with README.md, metadata.json (timestamp "2026-10-31T02:00:10Z"), schema.sql, import.sql and data/*.csv (categories, crate_downloads, crates, ...). The README says the live version_downloads table covers 90 days and "All available historical data (back to November 2014) ... is available at https://static.crates.io/archive/version-downloads/ in CSV form", and warns that CSV fields contain user-supplied text unmodified. The page also documents the sparse index (index.crates.io), RSS feeds and the API. The Usage Policy names "the Rust Foundation as the official legal entity providing the crates.io service"; the Foundation is US-registered and is recorded as international-ngo, like other foundation-run global registries in this vertical.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: none found. The Data Access Policy page (https://crates.io/data-access) states access rules and rate limits but no licence; the dump README has no licence section; the Usage Policy (https://crates.io/policies) ends "Licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license", which applies to that policy document. Crate metadata is author-submitted, and the dump includes user names and GitHub logins. Treat re-use terms as unstated. Not checked: the full CSV list beyond the first few files, and the dump changelog (GitHub issue #3617).

entries.title: Stanford AI Index Report Public Data
entries.description: The chart data behind Stanford HAI's annual AI Index Report, a widely cited compilation of indicators on AI research and development, technical performance, responsible AI, the economy, science, medicine, education, policy and governance, and public opinion.
entries.publisher: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI), AI Index Steering Committee

coverage.spatial: global, with country comparisons
coverage.temporal: annual editions 2017-2026 (2020 not linked on the landing page); series start years vary

entries.license: unverified — the 2026 report PDF is "licensed under Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International" (CC-BY-ND-4.0); no separate licence was found for the public data folder, much of which compiles third-party sources
entries.attribution: Sajadieh, S., Fattorini, L., Perrault, R., Gil, Y., Parli, V., et al. "The AI Index 2026 Annual Report," AI Index Steering Committee, Institute for Human-Centered AI, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, April 2026. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2606.15708
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (read in headless Chromium). The 2026 report page links "Download the report" (https://hai.stanford.edu/assets/files/ai_index_report_2026.pdf, HTTP 200, about 38 MB) and "Access the Public Data", a Google Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1zJTOg0iR0j5SijCwFutwWvDt143lW277) titled "PUBLIC DATA: 2026 AI INDEX REPORT" with "Download all" and nine chapter folders ("1. Research and Development" to "9. Public Opinion"), all dated Apr 8. Google Drive is only Stanford's hosting choice; the publisher is Stanford HAI. The PDF says "The public data and high-resolution images of all the charts in the report are available on Google Drive." The AI Index landing page (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index) lists reports for 2017-2019 and 2021-2026. Stanford is a private university, not a government body; it is included as the one non-governmental AI source because the index is a research compilation, not company training or evaluation data. The file formats inside the chapter folders were not opened (only the PDF format is confirmed), and earlier editions' data links were not checked. Each new edition has a new URL, so this entry will need updating yearly.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the 2026 report PDF, "How to Cite This Report" page: "The AI Index 2026 Annual Report by Stanford University is licensed under Attribution-NoDerivatives 4.0 International." That covers the report; no licence file or statement was seen for the Drive data folder, and the report draws on third-party data providers, so the data's licence is left unverified.

It covers internet access and use, connected devices, e-commerce, government online services, digital skills, online security, privacy and trust, online work, AI adoption, and barriers to access.
entries.publisher: Statistics Canada

coverage.spatial: Canada (provinces; territories not covered)
coverage.temporal: survey iterations including 2018, 2020 and 2022 (2022 latest seen)

entries.license: Statistics Canada Open Licence
entries.attribution: Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Internet Use Survey, <reference date>
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium), the survey's record page (record number 4432), "Detailed information for 2022", "Status: Inactive", "Frequency: Occasional", "Data release - July 20, 2023; November 2, 2023". It says the 2022 CIUS "aims to measure the adoption and use of digital technologies by individual residents of Canada 15 years of age and over, living in the provinces", and that "The survey is built off the previous iterations of the CIUS, last conducted in 2018 and 2020." No reference period newer than 2022 was seen; "Status: Inactive" is read as applying to the 2022 cycle and was not confirmed to mean the survey has ended. The participant page https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/survey/household/4432 (HTTP 200, modified 2024-07-18) also describes the 2022 cycle. The data tables live on www150.statcan.gc.ca, which reset the connection to curl this session, so the tables, the formats, the API and the start year weren't checked, and format is left empty.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the Statistics Canada Open Licence (https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/terms-conditions/open-licence, HTTP 200) grants "a worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to: use, reproduce, publish, freely distribute, or sell the Information", and requires the notice "Source: Statistics Canada, name of product, reference date. Reproduced and distributed on an "as is" basis with the permission of Statistics Canada." The licence is confirmed.

entries.title: USPTO Open Data Portal (including PatentsView)
entries.description: The US Patent and Trademark Office's single home for its public patent and trademark data: bulk data products, patent application and file-wrapper APIs, office actions, PTAB and petition decisions, and, since 2026, the PatentsView disambiguated inventor, assignee and location tables and long-text files formerly on patentsview.org.
entries.publisher: United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)

access.auth_note: free USPTO.gov account with multi-factor authentication required to sign in since June 18, 2026; API key (linked to ID.me per the FAQ) needed for APIs
access.rate_limit: API rate limits and a weekly download quota exist per the ODP FAQ (values not read)

coverage.spatial: United States (USPTO filings, applicants worldwide)
coverage.temporal: varies by product (PatentsView granted-patent tables from 1976 on the legacy site; not re-checked)

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: Source: United States Patent and Trademark Office, www.uspto.gov
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl; the portal is a JavaScript app and was read in headless Chromium). It shows "Open Data Portal Registration Requirement: In order to access the Open Data Portal (ODP), starting on June 18, 2026, you'll need to sign in with a valid USPTO.gov account", with MFA required, and says API keys for accounts missing profile fields "have been deactivated" since October 8, 2026. Dataset pages such as https://data.uspto.gov/bulkdata/datasets/pvgpatdis now redirect to a sign-in dialog, so no dataset content was read. https://patentsview.org/ answers 301 to https://data.uspto.gov/support/transition-guide/patentsview (HTTP 200), which says "The legacy PatentsView website (www.patentsview.org) is migrating to the USPTO's Open Data Portal (https://data.uspto.gov) starting on March 20, 2026". It maps the granted-patent and pre-grant tables (g_patent, g_cpc_current, g_assignee_disambiguated, claims and description text by year, sorted and annualized tables) to ODP bulk datasets pvgpatdis, pvgpattxt, pvpgpubdis, pvpgpubtxt, pvsorted and pva, so PatentsView is cataloged here rather than separately. The formats are assumed (PatentsView tables are CSV/TSV, bulk grants XML, APIs JSON) and weren't opened. The cadence describes the weekly bulk grant and application files; PatentsView tables update less often. Coverage start years weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no ODP-specific licence was found; the FAQ answers are collapsed and weren't expanded. USPTO's Terms of Use for USPTO websites (https://www.uspto.gov/terms-use-uspto-websites, HTTP 200) says "Pursuant to federal law, most government-produced materials appearing on this website are not subject to copyright restrictions within the United States and are therefore in the public domain", asks for acknowledgement ("Source: United States Patent and Trademark Office, www.uspto.gov"), and notes "The USPTO reserves the right to assert copyright protection internationally." This is site-wide wording, not a data-specific licence. The PatentsView tables were historically built by contractors for USPTO, and the legacy patentsview.org site carried its own licence statement, which can no longer be read there. The licence for those tables is therefore less certain than for USPTO's own bulk data.

entries.title: WIPO IP Statistics Data Center

It is the standard source for cross-country patent counts.
entries.publisher: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)

coverage.spatial: Global (national and regional IP offices; applicant origin countries)
coverage.temporal: varies by indicator (historical data sets before 1980 published separately)

entries.license: WIPO IP Statistics Data Center conditions of use (free access; no republication or commercial resale of the datasets; cite "WIPO Statistics Database")
entries.attribution: WIPO Statistics Database
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (curl). The page is a JavaScript app that client-side routes to https://www3.wipo.int/ipstats/key-search/indicator, and it was read in headless Chromium: "WIPO IP Statistics Data Center Source: WIPO statistics database. Last updated: May 2026", with tabs for Key indicators, Country profiles, Patent, Trademark, Industrial design, Utility model, Geographical indications, PCT, Madrid and Hague. The WIPO IP statistics landing page (https://www.wipo.int/ipstats/en/, which redirects to https://www.wipo.int/en/web/ip-statistics/, HTTP 200) calls the Data Center "a free online service" where users can "view or download both the latest and historical data", and links World Intellectual Property Indicators 2025 (2024 data). The download formats weren't checked (the FAQ mentions downloaded files opened in MS Excel), so format is left empty. No API was found.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the Data Center's About page (https://www.wipo.int/en/web/ip-statistics/about) says under "Conditions of use": "By using WIPO's statistical data, users agree not to republish or commercially re-sell WIPO's statistical datasets. In addition, when employing WIPO's statistics data in any written work, users shall cite "WIPO Statistics Database" as the source of the data." This is a service-specific condition and is not an open licence. WIPO's general Terms of Use (https://www.wipo.int/en/web/terms-of-use, not read directly; per search results) put new WIPO publications under CC BY 4.0, which covers reports such as World IP Indicators but not, on the evidence seen, the datasets.
